scenarios.title: Pinch with a visible cover
scenarios.objective: Join the attack only when the high cover and puck route support the pinch.
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks the Gold net. YOU is near the offensive blue line with D2 high support; F1 carries below and Gold has two defenders between the puck and net. The rep is a declared cover decision, not a promise of a successful pinch.
cues: The puck is loose below YOU.
The cover is a stated practice condition, not an outcome.

questions.prompt: What is directly stated about the high cover?

options.text: D2 is the named high support

questions.explanation: D2 is identified as high support; the loose puck and still frame do not prove a completed pinch.

questions.prompt: Which two checks belong before stepping down?

options.text: Whether D2 can cover behind YOU
Whether F1 can keep or recover the puck
Whether the blue line itself makes the pinch safe

questions.explanation: Cover and puck access explain why the pinch may fit; the line alone does not remove the recovery risk.

questions.prompt: Arrange a supported-pinch read.

options.text: Check D2 and the puck route
Step down while D2’s cover still protects the recovery lane
Re-check the puck and high space

questions.explanation: The cover and route set the conditions; the final scan decides whether to continue or recover.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to a conservative high position with D2 visible.
questions.explanation: This keeps YOU near the line while preserving the high support relationship.

questions.prompt: D2 is pulled low by a changing puck route. What should YOU reconsider?

options.text: Hold high or recover until cover is restored
Pinch farther because D2 is busy
Assume F1 will win the puck

questions.explanation: D2 no longer covers the same space, so the safer branch is to preserve the line or recover while scanning F1.

questions.prompt: Which three cues make this pinch supported rather than merely aggressive?
questions.explanation: Name D2 as the cover, the reachable puck route, and the recovery lane. If either support cue disappears, keep the blue line protected.

scenarios.title: Draw one penalty killer
scenarios.objective: Move the puck to shift one penalty killer while keeping a second receiver available.
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks the Gold net on a power play. YOU has the puck near the right half wall; F2 is low, F3 is inside, and Gold 1 is between YOU and F2. The scene gives a local passing choice, not a prescribed formation.
cues: YOU owns the puck at the half wall.
Gold 1 sits between YOU and F2.

questions.prompt: Which player currently owns the puck?
questions.explanation: The setup assigns the puck to YOU, so the local read starts from the half wall.

questions.prompt: Which two cues support moving the puck?

options.text: The power play fixes every receiver in place

questions.explanation: Coverage and support make the puck move useful; the structure still changes as Gold shifts.

questions.prompt: Arrange a local power-play read.

options.text: Identify the pressure and two receivers
Move the puck to change the coverage

questions.explanation: The pass is a tool to move coverage, then the new lane must be read again.

questions.prompt: Move YOU a little toward the blue line along the half wall to compare a different diagonal to F3.
questions.explanation: Backing along the wall changes the diagonal around Gold 1 while keeping both receivers in view. It illustrates an angle change, not a guaranteed open pass; recheck the defender and F3 before using it.

questions.prompt: Gold 1 commits toward F2 after your angle change. What deserves a fresh check?

options.text: Whether F3 or the original wall lane is now reachable
Force F2 because the defender moved
Stay on the same angle without scanning

questions.explanation: Gold 1's commitment changes both receiving relationships; choose only after checking the new lane.

questions.prompt: Name the half-wall space and explain how changing your angle can affect two receivers.
questions.explanation: The half wall gives YOU a carrier reference; changing the line can pull Gold 1 and expose F3 or F2, depending on which route stays open.

scenarios.title: Shift the penalty kill toward the new side
scenarios.objective: Exchange a flank responsibility while keeping the slot protected.
scenarios.briefing: Gold attacks the Navy net on a penalty play. YOU is low on the right side, D1 protects inside, and Gold 1 has the puck high left. Gold 2 is opposite and can become the next receiver.
cues: Gold 1 has the puck high left.
YOU is responsible for a changing low-side relationship.

questions.prompt: Which team is YOU defending in this setup?
questions.explanation: YOU is navy and Gold has the puck, so this is a defensive read.

questions.prompt: Which two cues matter during a flank-to-flank shift?
questions.explanation: Inside support and the next receiver guide the exchange; the puck side can change the task.

questions.prompt: Which order keeps the slot protected during the flank shift?

options.text: Name the puck side and slot

questions.explanation: The shift preserves the slot while the puck and receiver move across the picture.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to a more central low-slot cover position.
questions.explanation: This places YOU nearer the inside lane and keeps the puck side in view.

questions.prompt: Gold passes across to Gold 2. What should you check first?

options.text: Whether D1 and YOU still cover the inside lane
Leave the slot to follow the pass

questions.explanation: The cross-ice pass changes the coverage picture; protect the inside lane while deciding who takes the new carrier.

questions.prompt: Why can a penalty kill not cover every pass at once?
questions.explanation: Players must protect the most dangerous reachable lane and communicate exchanges. When Gold moves the puck, the coverage relationship changes and needs a new scan.

scenarios.title: Recover the power-play draw
scenarios.objective: Read possession after a power-play draw before choosing retrieval or support.
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks the Gold net on a power play. The draw has sent the puck loose near the right circle; YOU is closest, F2 is low support, and Gold 1 closes from above.
cues: The puck is loose after the draw.

questions.prompt: Has Navy secured the puck yet?
questions.explanation: The puck has no owner in the setup, so the draw has not established possession.

questions.prompt: Which two priorities belong in the retrieval?

options.text: The faceoff label guarantees a clean win

questions.explanation: Pressure and support shape the retrieval; the draw result must still be read.

questions.prompt: Arrange a possible start after the draw.

options.text: Find the loose puck and pressure
Check F2 and the exit again

questions.explanation: The route begins with the actual loose puck and updates after control.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to an approach angle near the puck-side circle with F2 visible.
questions.explanation: This point approaches the puck while leaving F2 and Gold 1 in the scene.

questions.prompt: Gold 1 reaches the puck first. What is useful now?

options.text: Switch to pressure or support based on the new carrier

questions.explanation: Gold possession changes the job. Re-scan the carrier and the next defensive lane.

questions.prompt: How does F2 change the recovery choice after the draw?
questions.explanation: F2 can support the pickup or become the outlet, depending on who controls the puck and where Gold 1 closes.

scenarios.title: Replace high support after entry
scenarios.objective: Fill a changed high support role without crowding the puck carrier.
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks Gold’s net. After F2 receives the entry pass, YOU are on the wall side of F2 and F3 supports lower in the zone. Gold 1 and Gold 2 defend inside while D1 is nearer the blue line. The next support job depends on F2 and those defenders.
cues: F2 owns the puck after the stated entry pass.
YOU is the high support option.

questions.prompt: After the entry pass, which Navy player is the carrier?
questions.explanation: The setup assigns possession to F2 after the entry pass.

questions.prompt: Which two details matter when filling high support?

options.text: A high support spot chosen without checking F2’s lane

questions.explanation: Support follows the carrier and coverage; a fixed spot can crowd or disconnect the play.

questions.prompt: Arrange the post-entry support change.

options.text: Find F2 and the inside coverage

questions.explanation: The support lane is useful only if it remains reachable from F2.

questions.prompt: Move YOU into a high-slot support example after F2 receives.
questions.explanation: This gives F2 a higher connection while keeping the defenders visible.

questions.prompt: F2 loses the puck to Gold 2. What takes priority?

options.text: Re-read the transition and recover toward the dangerous lane
Assume the entry is still controlled

questions.explanation: Possession changed, so the role changes before the old support route is continued.

questions.prompt: Which support space did YOU fill, and what route does it leave F2?
questions.explanation: A separated high-slot lane gives F2 a visible outlet or room to carry. If Gold closes it, re-offer from another reachable angle.

rows.reason: F2 is the current puck owner in both the setup and briefing after the stated entry pass. The keyed choice distinguishes F2 from F3 and YOU without relying on a later hypothetical.

F2's puck position and the two visible Gold inside defenders are the relevant support checks. The fixed high spot alternative is a credible failure because the briefing makes support depend on F2's lane.

The coaching sequence starts with the actual carrier and inside coverage, offers a separated lane, then rechecks F2 and the exit. It is explicitly a suggested routine rather than a mandatory scored order.

The reference (20.5,4) is a high-slot support example from YOU at (20,8), with F2 at (19,0), D1 near the blue-line side at (10,4), and both Gold defenders visible. The explanation correctly leaves timing and lane choice conditional.

If Gold 2 takes possession from F2, the keyed response correctly changes from offensive support to a transition recovery read. Waiting for F2 or assuming continued control are distinct stale-possession errors.

The explanation names the separated high-slot support relationship and the route it can leave for F2, then requires a fresh offer if Gold closes it. It does not claim that the illustrated point guarantees an outlet.

findings.issue: q4 claims to open a diagonal lane to F3, but its reference barely moves YOU and remains on the upper wall rather than illustrating a meaningful line toward F3.
findings.evidence: YOU starts at (18,9), F3 is at (21,-1), and the reference is (19.5,8.1); the direct line toward F3 is substantially lower, so the stated diagonal change is not represented.
findings.recommendedChange: Move the reference into a clearly different angle toward F3, for example {x:19.5,y:4}, while checking it does not collide with Gold 1 or F2; or change the prompt to a small half-wall angle adjustment. Rehash q4.

rows.reason: With Navy attacking toward positive x, moving YOU from (18,9) to (16,9) is a small blue-line-side adjustment along the half wall. The explanation correctly frames it as an angle comparison around Gold 1, not a guaranteed pass, and names the required recheck.
